title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the first labour print of 2027 and the first whose AWE window is wholly post-Budget
source: EST: two UK-government primaries fetched direct 2026-09-09, both HTTP 200. (1) gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-january-2027 — the statutory pre-announcement register reads 'UK Labour Market: January 2027', '19 January 2027 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics. (2) ons.gov.uk/releases/uklabourmarketjanuary2027 — the ONS release-calendar entry reads 'UK Labour Market: January 2027', 'Release date: 19 January 2027 7:00am', marked 'This release is not yet published.' Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap the 2026 siblings were filed under. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of uk-labour-market-2026-12-15, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-labour-market-2026-12-15 LANE, 2026-09-09. Why it earns a slot rather than waiting for the next sweep: it is the release that closes the question this calendar's four 2026 labour entries have all had to defer. Applying the publication pattern this lane verified across three bulletins fetched today — each carries the three months ending two months before its release month (March 2026 release: Nov-Jan; June: Feb-Apr; August: Apr-Jun) — the January 2027 release carries Sep-Nov 2026 AWE/LFS, Oct-Dec vacancies and the December payroll flash. Sep-Nov 2026 is still NOT wholly post-Budget (September closes before 2026-10-28); the first AWE window that is wholly post-Budget is Nov-Jan, which publishes in the FEBRUARY 2027 release, and even that would show nothing on the 2024 precedent that UK employer-cost measures take effect the following April. The honest reason this entry matters is narrower and it is calendrical: it is the first labour read after the 2026-12-17 MPC vote and the last before the 2027-02-04 round, which the Bank's own upcoming-MPC-dates page (fetched 2026-09-09) lists as PROVISIONAL and pairs with a Monetary Policy Report — so this print is the first observation against whatever the December minutes said and the first input to a forecast round. Tiered LOW on the same argued grounds as its 2026 siblings: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol, no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, and the measured cable reaction to the 2026-08-18 release was ~0.1% on a two-sided beat. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
